title: The Best Strategy in Reality Fracture Draft!
event: FRA early access / preview event (he thanks Wizards for free preview access at 0:04-0:09 'so I could get this recorded early'; live pod, the client shows 'Waiting on other players to pass a draft pack' between some picks; Premier / Quick not named on screen)
source: frames read from data/videos/raw/55awKvGIxRE (banner, pack grids and title strips every pick, pool/deck count at P1p7, P2p1, P3p1 and the deck builder); every pack list read from images that loaded (no placeholders); takes confirmed by the pool and the deck builder (all 42 picks accounted for: 23 spells, 4 nonbasic lands, the picked Island and Mountain among the free basics, 13 in the sideboard); transcript from YouTube auto captions, card names corrected against the dataset; nothing past 23:19 read; the game starts after 23:38

colour_path.quote: Let's take the anguish. It feels like a more unique effect.
why would I dip into a second color when I don't have to?
we have four great red cards, three good blue cards
I'm suspecting that I might end up having to splash because it's looking like I'm getting a little bit cut here and black is looking wide open.
So, red ends up maybe being the splash in a blue black deck.
I think blue black is the most likely now with maybe a red splash.
Blue red is kind of back on the menu this pack.
Blue Red is definitely on the menu. We do have these lands to help with splash black if needed.
Because we took the fixing lands, we get to take null summoner on the splash.

colour_path.main: UR splash B (Null Summoner, Extended Absence)
colour_path.quote: I think adding the two unsummons is going to help my early game as well.

picks.reasoning: Ajani's Anguish (rare): X damage to any target is removal early and a finisher late, and giving the team trample is real. He calls Campus Crier the common he would take and rates Rewrite Regrets and Generous Revival; between Crier and Anguish he takes the more unique effect.

considered.Campus Crier: probably the common he would take from this pack
considered.Rewrite Regrets: has been impressed, a card he is glad to draw in grindy matchups

quotes: between Campus Crier and Ajani's Anguish probably. Let's take the anguish. It feels like a more unique effect.
it's not the most powerful if you're just doing it early game because you'd rather have the common that deals three and empowers Jace one.

picks.reasoning: Violent Echoes: kill a three-toughness creature and draw a card. In this format he often takes a second good card of the colour of his first, and he already has Ajani's Anguish. Without it he would take Mindseeker Oculus.

considered.Mindseeker Oculus: would take it if Echoes were not here; 'I love this card'
considered.Arni, Humble Scribe: he has been overrating it, probably worse than Oculus; he keeps taking it and losing games
considered.Countersculpt: pretty good, but Empower Jace 1 is a little worse than a 1/1

quotes: I think I'm just going to take Violent Echoes. If this wasn't in the pack, I would just take Mindseeker Oculus.
Arni, who I think I've been overrating. ... I feel like I keep taking it and then losing games.

picks.reasoning: No Admittance over Repurposed Enforcer: with two red cards already, No Admittance locks him into red, and he asks why dip into a second colour when he does not have to. He calls Enforcer really strong and notes that three red cards and green cards (Marwyn, Bestial Incursion) are in the pack; he takes the safe option and admits he could be too greedy for the power card.

considered.Repurposed Enforcer: really strong aggressive two-drop; 'how am I getting it third'

quotes: like why would I dip into a second color when I don't have to?
Let's just take no admittance and take the safe option. It could be that I'm just like being too greedy here and maybe I'm just supposed to take the really powerful card.

picks.reasoning: Ruric Thar, Biomagus over Koth, the Geomancer, Vraska's Final Mercy and Break Under Pressure: he already has kill effects and wants a top-end card. Koth is guaranteed to make his deck but Ruric matters more: it felt amazing when he cast it and bad when the opponent did. 'We'll live a little' (blue).

considered.Koth, the Geomancer: solid, ping damage and ramp, guaranteed to make the deck
considered.Vraska's Final Mercy: pretty good but he has kill effects

picks.plan: Red with a blue top-end card; sees red and white flowing.
quotes: I just feel like Koth doesn't matter as much as Ruric Thar. I feel like every time I cast this card, I felt amazing when my opponent cast it, I feel pretty bad.
Let's take Ruric Thar. We'll live a little.

picks.reasoning: Pia, Determined Rebuilder: a 2/2 that makes a 1/1 flier, a card that comes in with value and is guaranteed to make the deck, over Liliana the Repentant (return a creature at six mana, a two-drop that mills before then). He also likes Unsummon and has just taken a blue card.

considered.Liliana the Repentant: good, but he already took a blue card and prefers a guaranteed playable to a black card
considered.Unsummon: likes it, good blue cards in the pack
considered.Koth, the Geomancer: 'we could have had Koth' from the previous pack, pretty solid

quotes: I think this being a two two that makes a one-one flyer is just really nice.
Taking a black card when we could just take a card that's guaranteed to make our deck.

picks.reasoning: Traxos, Academy Guardian: 'play No Admittance into Traxos on turn four and you've really done it'. Mabel, Valley Hero is also good and a red-white deck was possible, but he already has Ruric Thar and does not need to deviate.

considered.Mabel, Valley Hero: pretty good, still in the pack; could have built red-white

quotes: I love me a Traxos. Traxos is so good. You just play like no admittance into Traxos on turn four, you've really done it.
Maybe we could have built a red white deck here, but we already have the Ruric Thar. No need to like deviate from that.

picks.reasoning: Surveillance Phantasm over Yuriko, Hope from the Shadows: a nice two-drop with late-game utility that works with Empower Jace and he can attack with. Yuriko is situational and legendary. Mabel, Bitter Recluse is the best card in the pack but no red is left and he has four red and three blue cards, so he does not need playables; he is filling the curve, and the Phantasm is an artifact that goes with Pia.

considered.Yuriko, Hope from the Shadows: situational; he would play it but it is legendary
considered.Mabel, Bitter Recluse: best card in the pack but not his colours
considered.Rank Rat: black card, he wants blue here

picks.plan: Red-blue: four great red cards, three good blue cards.
quotes: Surveillance Phantasm is just like a nice two drop creature. Gives you some late game utility.
we're not going to have to worry about like getting playables at this point.

picks.reasoning: Extended Absence, the black card, over Whiplash Wordsmith and Afterthought Sentry; he does not want a random two-drop that can gain flying. Red is closing up (Wordsmith that late), and he thinks the neighbour passing this pack is not red.

considered.Afterthought Sentry: 'a random two drop that can gain flying. I just don't like this one very much'

picks.plan: Red-blue; red may be drying up.
quotes: So, I guess we'll just take the black card here.
Red's closing up a little bit, but we got so many good red cards early ... I imagine the first store left probably isn't in red. They might have gotten into blue. Pack two should be good to us.

picks.reasoning: Stingerquill Annex (land) over Surveillance Phantasm, Rewrite Regrets and Campus Crier on the wheel: he would rather take the Phantasm, but the land could help splash Extended Absence, and he suspects he will end up splashing because he is getting cut and black looks wide open.

considered.Surveillance Phantasm: wanted it over the land, two-drop

picks.plan: Red-blue with a possible black splash.
quotes: The land could help me splash absence, but do I really want to splash absence? Not really. I'd rather just play like a two-color deck, but I'll take the land here.
I'm suspecting that I might end up having to splash because it's looking like I'm getting a little bit cut here and black is looking wide open.

picks.reasoning: Countersculpt over Arni, Humble Scribe: he has learned that Arni is a little worse than he thinks, and Countersculpt is a good card that also empowers Jace.

considered.Arni, Humble Scribe: worse than he thinks it is

quotes: Let's take the counter sculpt over the Arni. I think I'm just going to learn that lesson and be like, you know, Arni is a little worse than I think it is.

picks.reasoning: Theorix Charm (blue-black gold) over Sphinx's Approach, Predictive Preparations and Theoretical Necromancer; no comment on the card itself, his only remark is that blue-black vibes are coming.
picks.plan: Blue-black vibes; red maybe the splash.
quotes: Yeah. So, it's looking like we're going to get some blue black vibes coming our way.

picks.reasoning: Icy Reception over Void Extrapolator: another counter spell, though he is not really liking the counter spell very much; Extrapolator has been pretty decent too.
picks.plan: Blue base; red or black second.
quotes: Another counter spell over the void extrapolator. I'm not really liking the counter spell very much. It's okay, but I think the extrapolator's been pretty decent, too.

picks.reasoning: Unsummon over Icy Reception: he likes Unsummon and has too many counter spells anyway.
quotes: I get unsummon now. I like the unsummon. Only too many of the counter spell anyway.

picks.reasoning: Last card, Traxos, Scourge Eternal, auto-picked. He says 'we get the Traxos here' and that red may end up the splash in a blue-black deck.
picks.plan: Blue-black with a red splash (at this point).
quotes: And we get the Traxos here. So, red ends up maybe being the splash in a blue black deck.

picks.reasoning: Sphinx of False Conclusions: flash it in, block, and you have another creature as a 4/2 flier; easy to kill but even then you are up a resource. 'We'll take the Sphinx here', blue-black now most likely with maybe a red splash. He says two cards (Kiora, Clash of Elements) are fine splash cards he does not want to splash. He notes he got a little punished for first-picking Ajani's Anguish; without it he would have left red sooner.

considered.Kiora of Fire and Ashes: a fine splash card, does not want to splash it
considered.Clash of Elements: fine splash card, does not want to splash it

picks.plan: Blue-black with maybe a red splash.
quotes: We don't really want to play just a straight Grixis deck, but we'll take the Sphinx here. I think blue black is the most likely now with maybe a red splash.
if I hadn't first picked a Ajani's Anguish, I probably would have moved off of red a little sooner.

picks.reasoning: Ruric Thar, Biomagus again: only two black cards so far, so he keeps taking blue; he wants to lock up his finishers because he sometimes takes too many cheap cards and lacks them. Winter is pretty good; he sees another Countersculpt.
quotes: I still do only have like two black cards, so I'm still just trying to take blue cards. I think here, let's just take another Ruric Thar. Just great top end card.
I think sometimes I take too many cheap cards and I don't have enough finishers.

picks.reasoning: Traxos, Academy Guardian second copy, because blue is now his main colour, over Heartstring Puller, another Icy Reception (he does not really want more than one) and Silence the Echo. He does not want too many more because they are legendary.

considered.Icy Reception: does not want more than one Icy Reception, really ever
considered.Traxos, Scourge Eternal: a copy is in the pack

quotes: Just absolutely love Traxos. I'm going to take that cuz blue is my like main color now.
I don't really want more than one icy reception really ever
We have a couple copies now. I don't want too many more because they're a legendary.

picks.reasoning: Innovative Commons (land) over Protege's Awakening and Fblthp: he is almost certainly going to splash and the land really helps; he says lands fill a unique role because you cannot get them in other spots, and hopes to get Awakening and Fblthp later.

considered.Protege's Awakening: 'a great card', has been annoyed when opponents play it
considered.Fblthp, Impossibly Lost: does not love it; hopes they come later

picks.plan: Splashing; fixing for a black or red splash.
quotes: I might just take this land though because I am going to almost certainly be splashing and just the land really helps.
Lands fill a very unique role in limited. You just can't get them in other spots.

picks.reasoning: Cryotheory Adept: a two-drop for the deck; the alternative was to splash green for Mind Meanderer, a nice top-end card, but his top end is sorted already (one reason he prioritised it). He expected Adept to be meh, but prowess goes a long way.

considered.Mind Meanderer: nice top-end card but he would have to splash green and his top end is sorted
considered.Cryotheory Adept: pretty reasonable, playing it has been fine

picks.plan: Blue-red or blue-black with a splash.
quotes: We'll get a two drop for our deck. Or we could try to splash green Mind Meanderer is a nice top end card. I kind of already have my top end sorted though.
Honestly, I've been pretty fine playing this one. I thought it would be kind of meh, but the prowess goes a long way.

picks.reasoning: Clash of Elements: blue-red is back on the menu from this direction. He has two black cards 'just chilling' and counts four good red removal spells.
picks.plan: Blue-red again; black two cards as splash.
quotes: So currently I just have these two black cards just chilling. Blue red is kind of back on the menu this pack. I kind of expect the blue red to be good from this direction and it definitely has been.
Sphinx was a great pickup. Anguish. I mean, we have one, two, three, four good red removal spells.

picks.reasoning: Theorix Annex (blue-black land), a black source for the splash: pack 2 is going well for his blue-red deck but pack 3 may get dicey, and every black source helps him play extra Theorix Charms and Extended Absences. Frostbite Pyromental and Winter, Team Player are also in the pack.
quotes: It's very aggressive. I'm more mid-rangey. I'm just going to take this card. I think help me with my black splash.
every black source just helps me play like extra Theorix charms, extra extended absences.

picks.reasoning: Unsummon (second copy): with two Unsummons he can prioritise card draw higher; he has no pure card-draw spells yet. Winter is fine but hard to fit into a deck that is both convoking and has many non-creatures.

considered.Winter, Team Player: 'fine', hard to find a deck that convokes and has a lot of non-creatures

quotes: Maybe I'll take another unsummon and just like when you have two unsummons, you then just can prioritize card draw a little bit higher.
I don't love Winter. He's fine, but it's hard to find a deck that is simultaneously convoking and has a lot of non-creatures.

picks.reasoning: Clash of Elements wheeled and he takes the second copy. Blue-red is definitely on the menu, with lands to splash black if needed; he counts 18 playables, none bad.
quotes: We wield Clash of Elements, so I'm liking that. Blue Red is definitely on the menu. We do have these lands to help with splash black if needed.
currently just blue, red, 18 playables here. None of these cards are bad.

picks.reasoning: Fatehold Chronologist: he could also take Sphinx's Approach for pure card draw to supplement the Unsummons, but does not mind a Chronologist; later he says he is not the biggest fan of it.

considered.Sphinx's Approach: could take for pure card draw
considered.Fatehold Chronologist: could be good; not the biggest fan though

quotes: Fate hold chronologist could be good. Sphinx's approach I could also take for pure card draw to kind of supplement the unsummons, but I don't mind getting a chronologist, I don't think.

picks.reasoning: Heartstring Puller over Icy Reception: he loves it and blue-red looks open from this direction; he only really wants one Icy Reception and already has one.
quotes: I love this guy. Blue red's looking open. And then I only really want one of these.

picks.reasoning: Protege's Awakening over Fblthp: he can afford it now; he may not have the creatures to pressure and draw with it but can bounce their stuff to draw cards.
quotes: Okay, Prodigy's Awakening. I think I can afford to take now over Fibble. I might not have the creatures to pressure to draw with this, but I might be able to like bounce their stuff to draw cards with this

picks.reasoning: Fatehold Annex (blue-white land) over Blazing Crescendo, as a speculative land: maybe a weird world where a white card is wanted, though he would not want many white cards.
quotes: blazing crescendo. No, let's just take the blue white land. Maybe there's a weird world. We get a white card we really want. Not that there's a lot of white cards I would really want.

picks.reasoning: Last card, Island, auto-picked.

Null Summoner on the splash: because he took the fixing lands, he can take it; he thinks it is really, really strong and has the blue-black lens to support it, so two Swamps in the deck are enough. Protege's Awakening may wheel and so may Infinite Coursework.
picks.plan: Blue-red splashing black for Null Summoner.
quotes: Because we took the fixing lands, we get to take null summoner on the splash. I think this card is just really, really strong.
I have the blue black lens to support it. So I can just throw two swamps in there, get this guy in the deck.

picks.reasoning: Surveillance Phantasm over Break Under Pressure: he says this pack is not going to be good for blue-red but the previous one gave him what he needs; he has enough kill (two Clash of Elements, No Admittance, Violent Echoes) and does not need more kill spells, especially splashed ones, so another two-drop with late-game applications.

considered.Break Under Pressure: removal, but not needed; kill count already four

quotes: I could just take surveillance phantasm. I have this. So what's my kill count look like? I have two Clash of Elements, no admittance, violent echoes. I don't really need more kill spells, especially splashed ones.
get myself another two drop that also has late game applications

picks.reasoning: Awaken the Inferno over Saheeli, Jewel of Avishkar and Theorist's Sanctum: Saheeli is very good, he considers floating it to wheel (20-30%), but he is not chaining spells and Awaken is a kill spell that also fetches black for Null Summoner.

considered.Saheeli, Jewel of Avishkar: really good, tried to float it hoping for a wheel
considered.Theorist's Sanctum: likes it as a late-game land

quotes: I think I might just want awaken the Inferno more as a kill spell. That also helps me get my black cards in order to get my null summoner more consistently.
I think I'm going to try to float this like because there's like a 20% chance I can wheel Saheeli.

picks.reasoning: Shipwreck Marsh (blue-black land) over Hapatra, the Desert Fang: he is already there on playables, the black lands are getting in, the charm and Chronologist might get in, his four-drop slot is crowded, and the land helps the splash further.

considered.Hapatra, the Desert Fang: could take it but is going to get there on playables already; four-drop slot crowded

quotes: Let's just take the land. I could take Hapatra, but I'm going to get there on playables already.
And the land just helps with my splash some more.

picks.reasoning: Twinned Vision over Perfected Theory and Apex Witchstalker: he says he will never cast the one card so he does not want it as a landcycler; Perfected Theory is fine. Maybe he wants Twinned Vision or not; he does not want two Chronologists.

considered.Apex Witchstalker: never going to cast it so does not want it as a land cycler

quotes: Okay, I'm never going to be able to cast this, so I don't want this as a land cycler. Perfected theory is fine. I'm just going to take Twin Division. Maybe I want it. Maybe I don't.

picks.reasoning: Plan for All Outcomes: there are a lot of really nice four-drops in blue and he has many blue-red four-drops; he hopes to cast it later as a five-drop double-spell turn. Pretty strong.
quotes: There's a lot of four drops in blue I'm noticing that are really, really nice.
Hopefully I can cast this a little bit later sometimes. Like five drop double spell thing. We'll take this card though. It's just pretty strong.

picks.reasoning: Mindseeker Oculus: 'love getting a Mindseeker Oculus'.
quotes: Love getting a Mindseeker Oculus.

picks.reasoning: Arni, Humble Scribe over Hallway Heckler: his three-drop slot needs extra juice and he thinks Arni is better than Heckler, despite his earlier opinion of it; he is glad he took Awaken the Inferno over Saheeli.

considered.Hallway Heckler: worse than Arni for this deck

quotes: Sure, I will take an Arni. Now, my three drop slot does need a little bit of extra juice, I think. I think it's better than hallway Heckler.
I'm actually feeling really glad that I took the Awaken the Inferno over Saheeli.

picks.reasoning: Protege's Awakening (another copy): he will not want it main-deck but might sideboard into more if a slower matchup arises.
quotes: Sure, I'll take another Protege's Awakening. I'm not going to want this card. And I maybe want to sideboard into more of these.

picks.reasoning: Divining Duelist; he says only that he takes it and then counts ('one, two, three, four, five') as the pack leaves.
quotes: Okay, we'll take the Divining Duelist

picks.reasoning: Undulating Witness, another landcycler; Saheeli did not wheel but that is fine.
quotes: Okay, cool. We get another land cycler. Saheeli did not wheel, but that's okay.

picks.reasoning: Paradox Shaper: a fine two-drop for the deck. He adds he is not surprised that Saheeli did not wheel and that the Awaken-over-Saheeli pick is one he would not have made in his first draft.
quotes: Paradox Shaper. It's going to be a fine two drop for my deck.

picks.reasoning: Perfected Theory (from Perfected Theory and Campus Crier); no comment in the transcript, the pick is confirmed by the sideboard at the end.
Last card, Mountain, auto-picked.
